title: XAUUSD bot for MT5 that reads Telegram signals and runs its own engines
author: Tidy_Si
selftext:
Hi all,

I've been working on this for a while as a personal project and it's got to the point where I think it needs people other than me poking at it.

It's an automated gold (XAUUSD) trader for MetaTrader 5, written in Python with a React dashboard that runs locally. Roughly what it does:

* **Reads Telegram signal channels** and turns posts like "Sell Gold 4520 - 4512" into structured trades. It handles edits (a lot of channels post the direction first and the levels a minute later), CLOSE ALL / BE / TP HIT style messages, and per-channel formats. When a channel changes format, an AI fallback extracts the levels and then generates a plain regex rule from the approved result, so it doesn't need the AI the next time. No AI-generated code ever runs, only pattern strings.
* **Runs two of its own signal engines**, completely isolated from each other: a breakout engine (break and go / break and retest) and a reversal engine that's an ICT / Smart Money emulation from plain OHLC (FVGs, inverted FVGs, liquidity sweeps, breaker blocks). Each has its own ML gate trained on its own closed trades.
* **Puts everything through the same risk pipeline** before it reaches the broker: freshness, reward:risk floor, correlation cap, session and news windows, then a risk governor that sizes from the real stop distance, with a daily loss halt and a loss-streak cooldown.
* **Manages the trade after entry**: TP ladder with partials, stop to breakeven, and a trailing stop that adapts to ATR/ADX and session.
* **Logs why it did everything.** For any trade you can see which signal it came from, which gates it passed, why it was sized that way and why it closed. There's also a decision log that records what currently-disabled gates *would* have done, so you can judge a filter against real trades before turning it on.

Runs on Windows natively, and on macOS via a Wine bridge to MT5.

**What I'm not going to do** is post results. It's not a "this makes X a month" thing, and I'd rather people judged the code and the logic.

**What I'd really like:**

* People to run it on a **demo account** and tell me what breaks, what's confusing to set up, and what's daft about the logic
* Opinions from anyone who's built ICT-style detection from OHLC
* Contributors, if anyone fancies it. There's a fairly strict test suite and some house rules in the repo, mainly because it touches real money

Repo: [https://github.com/MooreSi/forex-gold](https://github.com/MooreSi/forex-gold)

Please don't point it at a live account until you've watched it on demo for a good while. It places real orders.

Cheers

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: having the AI write a plain regex once a format is approved means it only touches each channel's format once, nice design. what happens when a channel edits its levels after you're already in?

replies.author: Tidy_Si
replies.body:
You could have IME (Immediate Market Entry) turned on which would execute a signal just based on a simple regex like "BUY NOW" or similar, a second follow-up message could parse the TP/SL and override the applied EA template levels. 

If there is a follow-up SL message there is an option to automatically apply the change in SL. With regards to an incorrect/malformed original signal that is then edited that could be added  easily with some examples.

  
Try it, see what you think and click the "Feedback" button to request a new feature, highlight a bug.

Cheers

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: so an edit after entry just becomes a modify on the open trade, nice. the one I'd still worry about is a channel deleting a signal they got wrong, since there's no follow-up message to parse.

replies.author: Tidy_Si
replies.body: No signals that are parsed to the EA are deleted/removed, that would be a manual process.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: ok so the gap is a provider who deletes or edits a call after posting it. the EA has already acted on the first version by then, so I'd at least log the original message id and flag it when the text changes.

replies.author: Tidy_Si
replies.body: Yes, correct. However, if this is a feature request I could add it. It could then with a toggle on/off automatically remove the executed trade (obviously risk) or send you a telegram alert asking what to do
